Messages.Author: Tom, Mad & Co
Messages.Body:
Hi all,

Since the last tournament rules, the fact that winning tables wa more
important than victory points has switched tournament play to, say, an
steadier mode.

Don't misunderstand me, i'm glad of that fact since the weenies and full
forward stealth-bleed or tap and bleed didn't give a chance to cross table
metagame, and now combat decks have (but just a little bit) more chance to
become tournament decks. But players, at least around here in spain, has
switched their games to a "catenaccio". I mean, bloat decks had seen some
kind of boost, as long as blockers like mono animalism, tzimi, and so. At
the last tournament we attended only 25% of the games ended on time,
throwing in the longest "half point" cards we've seen for long. We all
understand that the table points rule has developed the game to a more
"multiplayer" like level, but everyone is turning to decks that will bring
them to the end of a game, no matter if he only wins to victory points as
long as they give them a table point.

Discussing about this, someone reminded me that there was a "blood bank
limit" optional rule, something like 5 additional blood points per player in
the original rules.

So here is my proposal for discussion, may this rule be aplied to tournament
rules? I'm not sure if this will bring up another kind of metagame, but
surely will thwart some players for playing bloat/block decks or so.

At least, thanks to this rule, in the last Crusade: Hospitalet there were
weird decks in the final round: a warghoul deck, a salubri antitribu and a
brujah weenie deck (with not a few brujah debates). But the final round
lasted for more than 3 hours...

Tom,Mad&Co

Or ousting his prey, in wich case its pool will engross the blood bank. I
know that the 5 pool to blood bank per player will trail back to weenie
hordes, but that's what playtesting is about. Maybe a 10 pool add per player
will allow bloat, but will limit it to a lesser extend. If the blood
bocomes "scarce", the game will accelerate. If someone starts to bleed
heavily those pool will add to blood bank, so increasing the capability for
bloat decks or so to defend themeselves more properly. We play this game for
fun, at least most of us, and in the final round of that tournament, we all
get bored. If the players were bored, imagine the ones who were watching the
game.

I know this is not any panacea, but imho the way the tournament rules are
(which I prefer rather than the older ones) by now freezes the game.

Tom Mad&Co

Messages.Author: David Cherryholmes
Messages.Body:
On Thu, 6 Jun 2002, Tom, Mad & Co wrote:

<snip explanation of bled pool adding to bank>

Sorry, I missed the part about lost pool returning to the bank. That
changes things somewhat. Still, my experience doesn't gel with yours. I
don't see a problem with decks sitting on their hands and bloating out the
clock, either in casual play or the tournaments I've attended lately. If
there is a bloat-heavy, local metagame, then your proposal may very well
be a good fix, but I don't know how I'd test it. Further, I think it's
better to look for answers to metagame problems by using that metagame
against the people who insist on playing predictably[1]. Have you tried
playing a deck that bleeds well and maybe uses a high amount of Sudden
Reversals to counter the bloat?

[1] This is what I've tried to do as an answer to the Weenie Hordes of
Durham. In this case, I've still found that response to be
unsatisfying. I'm playing mostly nothing but vote-decks these days and
now have the joy of two or three opposing decks full of Delaying
Tactics. My enthusiasm for our weekly games is about snuffed out. Any
nuggets o' wisdom would be much appreciated.

David Cherryholmes
Prince of Durham

I've found something similar, but I was attributing it to players becoming more
cognizant of the multiplayer dynamic as it pertains to winning.

However, the table win system may have made a number of players more cognizant
of how to play to get more than one VP.

I can almost see why bloat would creep in, but excessive bloat really isn't
useful. You still gain more from ousting and dying than from not dying.

One answer may be trying to go with speed. See if you can oust a couple
players quickly before you burn out or get table managed to death. In an
environment with a lot of timed out games, just getting some VPs could get you
into the finals.

>Most of us have been playing this game since 95, and in tournaments since
>00. This is not the common metagame here basically because there is no
>standard metagame, whenever we play a few games we use different decks (I
>currently play a Cryptic mission deck, ahrimanes blocker, Palla grande tap
>and bleed, brujah debate with low caps, Masquerade
>enforcement-banishement-bloat deck and a true brujah combat). In tourneys,
>everyone brings up their steadier one, becoming every round a marathonian
>one.
>
>Has anybody tried to play with a blood bank limit? I just asked that

While at the same time that I could see people wanting to bloat rather than
draw the ire of the table, I've seen a drop off in massive bloat. Putting a
limit on the blood bank doesn't sound like it would matter to us.

What concerns me is how many decks get built that don't "know" how they are
going to oust their prey. Besides the problem of games not going anywhere*,
decks that don't go forward can cause seating position to become far too
important as the other common occurrence we see is lots of sweeps - the deck
with the ineffectual predator builds up to the point where it can roll over
everyone.

* We had a final where no one ousted as most of the decks simply weren't well
equipped at going forward and there was plenty of crosstable aid.

Atonement + Metro Underground is great for stopping weenies.
Good with Aabbt Kindred or disguised Sniper Rifles, works well with
the Victoria + Madness Network combo or even in a Smiling Jack deck.
I saw one guy use Atonement with Eagle's Sight and Millicent Smith to

(Defender of the Haven is AWESOME!). If Atonement's not your bag,
Justine, especially with a Sport Bike, can do wonders, and Eternal
Vigilance on Lazverinus is not half bad.

Are they weenie intercept hordes? If not (ie if your +1
stealth actions can usually get through), Atonement +
Flak Jacket (or Guardian Angel) should equal a lot of very
sad weenie decks. Need enough Wakes/other blocks to protect
the Atonement for a turn, of course. I'd go the Smiling
Jack route with this deck. Creepshow Casino might be good
for beating KRCG/etc if they start putting that in to try
to stop your Atonements.

Otherwise, I dunno. If you can't beat 'em, join 'em? A
weenie-heavy metagame may be hard to move in another
direction without just waiting for people to get tired of
playing weenies all the live-long day (or trying to talk
them into being tired of playing weenies all the live-long
day). After all, one of the major strengths of weenie decks
is that they don't have a lot of easily exploitable
weaknesses (sure, you can do anti-weenie stuff to 'em, but
they can always buy more weenies, it's not like they cost
much pool).

Josh

Stopping, or at least restricting, these kinds of interactions was an
explicit goal of the whole predator-prey business. "Sitzkreigs"
and neverending timeouts are an almost inevitable result of
a multiplayer game with negative interactions, 1 winner,
and unrestricted interactions. Between table wins and the superiority
of bloat over the measly 6 pool oust reward, the predator-prey
dynamic may no longer be strong enough to counter that drive.

Yup. I think I've homed in on the vote-thing just because this is a
method that makes 'em *all* hurt.

I'm a little embarassed to admit this for two reasons: A) it smacks of a
"moral authority" approach, and B) it seems to be a departure from "play
to win," a foundational assumption of the game (and an outright rule, for
tournament play). I have thought about it though, prior to this
thread-jack. "B" is easier to address, since the cross-table damage is
going to someone playing a deck with a basement-level pool investment and
I intend to kill them, too. The votes have been about 75%-ish
take-one-per-guy, and about 25%-ish KRC and I figure that extra three to
my prey and only my prey should make the trees fall about right.

"A" is pretty much impossible to justify to someone who doesn't already
share your opinion that weenies are bad for the game. I do see weenie
decks I like. One guy I play with has a weenie celerity deck that's kind
of neat, and when Jason Bell hit on the Sabbat babies making babies with
the Hungry Coyote trick, I was impressed with the power of it in a "isn't
that mushroom cloud pretty?" kind of way. The storyline tournament was a
snapshot of exactly what I'd like to see the game be. I don't really know
any way to do it, though; dictating what decks other people are allowed to
play now that the cards are out there is obviously bad. But whacking
people who can't step a little bit away from the "play to win" line and
towards the "play for fun" one in the head with a big stick seems to me a
little less obviously bad.

My apologies to the old-timers for beating a dead horse, but the issue
seems current and pertinent to me, and I know there's lots of good advice
out there to be had.

David Cherryholmes
Prince of Durham, NC
